headline: All majors below the 200-day line, momentum diverging, but whales moving Bitcoin off exchanges while stablecoins thin
paragraphs: The regime is fully bear-biased. Every major asset, without exception, sits below its 200-day moving average: Bitcoin at 48% below its 12-month high, Ethereum at 60%, Solana at 70%, and the worst performers like Cardano at 80% below theirs. No golden cross anywhere. This is not a contested regime, it is a settled one. The only technical wrinkle is momentum, which tells a different story. Bitcoin's RSI sits at 54.3, neutral territory, and its MACD is below signal, but Ethereum's RSI is 56.9, also neutral, while Cardano has climbed to 64.5 on an RSI that usually means overbought. More interesting: Binance and Dogecoin both have MACD above their signal lines, the only two among the majors doing so, yet neither is trading above the 200-day. This is a classic divergence, momentum trying to reset higher even as the larger trend stays down. Ether's move is the loudest: up 2.72% in the last 24 hours and up 15.24% over 30 days, yet it is still 60% underwater from its annual high. That spread between short-term momentum and long-term drawdown is worth watching.

Positioning in perpetual futures reveals heavy long bias and expensive funding in the majors. Bitcoin's 8-hour funding sits at 0.13%, which annualizes to 1.4%, mildly positive but not punishing. Ethereum is much spicier at 0.48% every eight hours, or 5.3% annualized, telling you that longs are paying a real premium to stay long. Solana and Dogecoin are both north of 5% annualized funding, also long-biased and pricey. The exception is XRP, which is paying shorts at negative 8.8% annualized funding, a signal that shorts have become crowded or that the market is pricing in a downside bias. Open interest is substantial across the board, Bitcoin at 2 billion dollars and Ethereum at 1.3 billion, meaning the boat is full. The long-short ratio tells you how full: Bitcoin has 1.27 longs per short, a modest edge, but Ethereum is at 1.69, Solana at 2.57, and Dogecoin at a wild 5.03 longs per short. When a crowd is this skewed to one side and paying to hold that bet, that is a crowded trade, not fuel. Liquidations in the last 21 to 23 hours have been asymmetric: shorts are getting wiped in Bitcoin and Ethereum (7.7 and 11.2 million dollars respectively over longs), but longs are taking the heat in XRP and Dogecoin. This is fragmentation, not consensus.

Flows reveal a tension between whale behavior and the traditional finance bid. Over the last 24 hours, 297.9 million dollars of Bitcoin moved off exchanges, a single-day print that sits within a wider context: the last four weeks of weekly net flows show three weeks of large outflows and one week with a 1.2 billion dollar inflow, so the weekly trend is mixed. The Bitcoin move off exchanges looks like cold storage accumulation, not panic selling. Meanwhile, stablecoin buying power has contracted by 1.16% over the last 30 days, and today's stablecoin float sits at 305.9 billion dollars, modest relative to Bitcoin's 2 trillion dollar market cap. The ETF picture is cleaner: Bitcoin spot ETF saw a 211.5 million dollar inflow on August 4th, and over the last five sessions has taken in 381.4 million dollars net. Ethereum's flows are lighter, 53.1 million on the day and 30.1 million over five sessions. The real money (ETF flows, whale cold storage moves) is directionally aligned toward accumulation, even as leverage is expensive and crowded in the opposite direction. That disagreement between price action (down for months) and the margin funding it costs (up, especially in Ethereum and Solana) is the tension of the day.

Sentiment is solidly fearful at 27 on the Fear and Greed gauge, sitting at the low end of a 20-to-33 range over the last 30 days. This is the crowd's emotional ceiling. Total market cap grew 0.88% to 2.3 trillion dollars, and Bitcoin dominance stands at 56.6%, stable and high. The small-cap tape is fractured: top gainers like BEAT, UB, and LIT are up 21%, 17%, and 6% respectively, noise at scale, while mid-tier names like PYTH, PUMP, and WLD are down 5% to 6%, also noise. Network fees on Bitcoin are at 3 to 4 satoshis per byte, lean, and difficulty has ticked up 1% with 429 blocks until the next retarget, a sign the network is running normally and miners are confident. The picture is one of fear without capitulation, momentum diverging from trend, positioning crowded and expensive, and quiet accumulation by large holders despite price weakness. None of this predicts the next move; it describes the balance of forces in the tape today.
